newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo says to expand collaboration with Mitsubishi.
newsitem.headline: Volvo says to expand collaboration with Mitsubishi.

text.p: Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo said on Wednesday it was expanding its collaboration with Mitsubishi Motors Corp in the technical development and production areas.
This will be through the two companies' NedCar joint venture in the Netherlands.

"To expand and augment the mutual benefits of this relatioship, the two companies have agreed to consider other opportunities for cooperation including the development of engine component technology and the joint development of future car platform to be produced at NedCar," Volvo Car Corp said in a statement.
Volvo said the two companies had recently signed a contract under which Mitsubishi will supply Volvo with the Gasoline Direct Injection (GDI) engine.
The GDI engine offers low fuel consumption and high power output. Mitsubishi is the first manufacturer to develop and use this engine technology.

"Mitsubishi will supply Volvo with GDI engines and transmissions for Volvo S40 and V40 models produced at NedCar, complementing the existing and planned engine progrmame previously envisaged for these vehicles," the statement said.
Volvo said the two companies were also conducting feasibility studies into two other key areas.
The first of these was the possible joint development of future car platform to be produced at NedCar.

"On the basis of the successful relationship established at NedCar, the two companies will commence studies for the next generation of cars beginning production at the start of the 21st century," the statement said.
Secondly they were looking at the incorporation of GDI technology.
"The two companies are currently also considering the possibility of the incorporation of GDI technology within the Volvo engine family," Volvo said.
"The increase in cooperation is seen as a natural expansion of the excellent collaboration between Mitsubishi Motors Corp and Volvo Car Corp originally started in 1991."
